QF.id: Retirement Planning Products: National Pension System (NPS)_61

question.text: Vikram, a private sector employee, has a basic salary of Rs.8 lakh and DA of Rs.2 lakh, and is taxed under the OLD tax regime. His employer contributes 12% of (Basic + DA) to NPS. What is the maximum amount deductible in Vikram's hands under Section 80CCD(2)?

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the old tax regime, NISM Series XVII workbook p. 144 caps the Section 80CCD(2) deduction for private sector employees at 10% of (Basic + DA). Basic + DA = Rs. 8 lakh + Rs. 2 lakh = Rs. 10 lakh. 10% of Rs. 10 lakh = Rs. 1,00,000. Even though the employer actually contributes 12% (Rs. 1,20,000), only Rs. 1,00,000 is deductible; the excess Rs. 20,000 is taxable as salary. The Trap: Option D (Rs. 1,40,000) is the defensible answer if the question is read under the new tax regime, because the same workbook page also refers to a 14% cap. The audit flagged this — the original stem did not specify the regime. Option C (Rs. 1,20,000) wrongly treats the full 12% employer contribution as deductible. Option A (Rs. 80,000) uses 8% with no source basis. Note: The original stem did not state the tax regime, leaving Rs. 1,00,000 (10% under old regime) and Rs. 1,40,000 (14% under new regime for certain employees) both defensible from p. 144. The stem now explicitly states the old tax regime, making option B uniquely correct.
